title: Precedent search over judgment records
body: Semantica exposes decisions as first-class objects with three READ operations: trace_decision_chain (causal ancestry of a decision), find_similar_decisions (precedent search), and impact analysis (what depends on this decision). Compose's judgment layer is strong on the write side — positions, amendments, ledger, goal/situation/person stores all shipped — but has no similarity-retrieval surface. This is the operation that makes recording pay for itself: you do not write judgment records to have them, you write them so the NEXT similar call retrieves the precedent unprompted. Two slices: (a) trace — walk the ledger to reconstruct the causal chain behind a position, mechanical, no embeddings needed; (b) precedent — semantic similarity over position statements, the natural bridge to the SmartMemory coupling (project_comp_smartmemory) since recall is exactly what SmartMemory is for. Slice (a) is worth doing standalone even if (b) never lands. Depends on IDEA-28 for correctness: a precedent is only useful if you can see what was believed AT the time it was decided, not what is believed now. NOTE: SmartMemory recall is currently unreliable (project_livefire_recall_broken, 19/20 drop) — do not build slice (b) on it until that is root-caused.
